title: What do we get from celebrity crushes? With Rebecca Tukachinsky Forster, PhD, and Karen Dill-Shackleford, PhD

sentences.en: Have you ever had a crush on someone you knew only through TV or the movies?
sentences.zh: 你曾经对一个只通过电视或电影认识的人动过心吗？

sentences.en: Maybe it was a famous actor or singer or even a fictional character.
sentences.zh: 也许是一个著名的演员、歌手，甚至是一个虚构的角色。

sentences.en: If so, you're not alone.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，你并不孤单。

sentences.en: Yes, researchers have studied this phenomenon, and they found the majority of adults say that they have had a celebrity crush.
sentences.zh: 是的，研究人员已经研究过这种现象，他们发现大多数成年人都表示自己曾对名人产生过倾慕之情。

sentences.en: These one-side emotional attachments are just one example of a parasocial relationship.
sentences.zh: 这些单方面的情感依恋只是准社会关系的一个例子。

sentences.en: More broadly, parasocial relationships are the relationships that people have with media figures, whether they're actors, celebrity influencers, or television characters.
sentences.zh: 更广泛地说，准社会关系是人们与媒体人物之间建立的关系，无论他们是演员、网红还是电视角色。

sentences.en: These kinds of relationships sometimes get a bad rap.
sentences.zh: 这类关系有时会背负不好的名声。

sentences.en: Remember the film Misery, in which Kathy Bates' character proclaims to the novelist, played by James Caan, I'm your number one fan?
sentences.zh: 还记得电影《危情十日》吗？凯西·贝茨饰演的角色对詹姆斯·凯恩饰演的小说家宣称：“我是你的头号粉丝。”

sentences.en: And we know how that turned out.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道结果如何。

sentences.en: But psychologists who study parasocial relationships say that they can be good for us.
sentences.zh: 但研究准社会关系的心理学家表示，它们对我们有益。

sentences.en: They can also help us expand our worldview and have positive effects on our mental health and well-being.
sentences.zh: 它们还可以帮助我们拓展世界观，并对我们的心理健康和幸福感产生积极影响。

sentences.en: So how is a parasocial relationship different from simply being a fan?
sentences.zh: 那么，准社会关系与单纯当粉丝有什么不同？

sentences.en: Can these relationships give us any benefits of real-life friendships?
sentences.zh: 这些关系能带给我们现实生活中友谊的任何好处吗？

sentences.en: Can they alleviate loneliness?
sentences.zh: 它们能缓解孤独感吗？

sentences.en: What happens when a parasocial relationship goes sour, when your favorite character or your celebrity crush disappoints you?
sentences.zh: 当准社会关系变质时会发生什么？当最喜欢的角色或让你倾慕的名人让你失望时呢？

sentences.en: Or even worse, how do these usually harmless relationships become obsessions?
sentences.zh: 或者更糟糕的是，这些通常无害的关系是如何变成痴迷的？

sentences.en: And how are these relationships changing now that social media gives us constant access to celebrities' lives?
sentences.zh: 既然社交媒体让我们能够持续接触名人的生活，这些关系又在发生怎样的变化？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，主要探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天请到了两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: First is Dr. Rebecca Tukashinsky-Forster, an associate professor in the School of Communication at Chapman University.
sentences.zh: 第一位是丽贝卡·图卡辛斯基-福斯特博士，她是查普曼大学传播学院的副教授。

sentences.en: She studies parasocial relationships and how people develop long-lasting, meaningful connections with media figures.
sentences.zh: 她研究准社会关系，以及人们如何与媒体人物建立持久、有意义的联系。

sentences.en: She's particularly interested in how parasocial romantic relationships develop and how they affect us.
sentences.zh: 她对准社会恋爱关系是如何发展的以及它们如何影响我们尤为感兴趣。

sentences.en: Dr. Tukashinsky-Forster is editor of the Oxford Handbook of Parasocial Experiences, published
sentences.zh: 图卡辛斯基-福斯特博士是《准社会体验牛津手册》的主编，该书于

sentences.en: this year by Oxford University Press, and author of the book, Parasocial Romantic Relationships,
sentences.zh: 今年由牛津大学出版社出版，她还是《准社会恋爱关系：

sentences.en: Falling in Love with Media Figures.
sentences.zh: 爱上媒体人物》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Next is Dr. Karen Dill Shackelford, a professor in the Department of Media Psychology at Fielding
sentences.zh: 接下来是卡伦·迪尔·沙克尔福德博士，她是菲尔丁

sentences.en: Graduate University.
sentences.zh: 研究生大学媒体心理学系的教授。

sentences.en: She's a social psychologist who studies pop culture and media in all its forms, particularly how being a fan or consumer of popular culture fiction affects people's well-being,
sentences.zh: 她是一名社会心理学家，研究各种形式的流行文化和媒体，特别是作为流行文化虚构作品的粉丝或消费者如何影响人们的幸福感、

sentences.en: empowerment, and positive belief change.
sentences.zh: 赋权和积极的信念改变。

sentences.en: She's editor of APA's journal, Psychology of Popular Media.
sentences.zh: 她是美国心理学协会期刊《大众媒体心理学》的主编。

sentences.en: Welcome to you both.
sentences.zh: 欢迎二位。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: I'm so excited.
sentences.zh: 我太激动了。

sentences.en: Let's start with a definition.
sentences.zh: 让我们从一个定义开始。

sentences.en: What are parasocial relationships and more specifically, how are they different from just being a fan of a celebrity or someone famous or prominent?
sentences.zh: 什么是准社会关系？更具体地说，它们与单纯成为某个名人或显赫人物的粉丝有什么不同？

sentences.en: Well, parasocial relationships is this, you described it so well, is this feeling of intimacy,
sentences.zh: 嗯，准社会关系就是这样一种——你刚才描述得太棒了——亲密感，

sentences.en: of knowing that media personality, that maybe it's a news anchor or a host of a television show that you see every day or once a week, and it can be a fictional character.
sentences.zh: 了解那个媒体人物，也许是一个你每天或每周看到一次的新闻主播或电视节目主持人，也可以是一个虚构的角色。

sentences.en: Someone that, by virtue of being exposed to them over and over, and hearing about their self-disclosures about their personal lives, you become like friends with them or develop
sentences.zh: 通过不断地接触他们，听他们进行关于个人生活的自我披露，你会觉得他们就像你的朋友，或者与他们发展出

sentences.en: other types of relationships with them that are one-sided, they are imaginary, but they are as real possibly for the person that experiences them.
sentences.zh: 其他类型的关系，这些关系是单方面的、想象出来的，但对经历它们的人来说，它们可能同样真实。

sentences.en: And it's kind of interesting to contrast it to fandoMs.
sentences.zh: 把这与粉丝群体进行对比是很有意思的。

sentences.en: First of all, fandom is not necessarily about a personality.
sentences.zh: 首先，粉丝群体不一定与某个特定人物有关。

sentences.en: You can be a fan of a show, for example, without feeling affiliation with any particular character on that show.
sentences.zh: 例如，你可以是一个节目的粉丝，但对该节目的任何特定角色都没有归属感。

sentences.en: But also, fandom is when something becomes an integral part of your identity.
sentences.zh: 而且，粉丝群体是指某种事物成为你身份不可分割的一部分。

sentences.en: When it becomes an important part of who you are and your self-definition.
sentences.zh: 当它成为你是谁以及你对自己的定义的重要组成部分时。

sentences.en: So, I would say some parasocial relationships are more like an acquaintance or a friend, but it's not rising to the level of being a fan.
sentences.zh: 所以，我会说有些准社会关系更像是熟人或朋友，但还没有上升到粉丝的程度。

sentences.en: Some researchers also talk about the distinction between parasocial relationships as you look
sentences.zh: 一些研究人员还谈到了准社会关系的区别，即你把

sentences.en: at the media personality as your peer, or maybe a super peer, but someone that is down-to-earth person.
sentences.zh: 媒体人物视为同龄人，或者超级同龄人，但认为他们是一个脚踏实地的人。

sentences.en: Whereas fandom, as you put that other celebrity or media personality on a pedestal, and you are, like, worshipping them, you are admiring them.
sentences.zh: 而粉丝群体则是你把另一个名人或媒体人物捧上神坛，你在崇拜他们，在仰慕他们。

sentences.en: So, they are nothing but...
sentences.zh: 所以，他们绝不是……

sentences.en: So, in some ways, they are the exact opposite of the down-to-earth person that you feel like you're having for dinner.
sentences.zh: 因此，在某些方面，他们和你觉得可以请来吃晚饭的那种脚踏实地的人完全相反。

sentences.en: And this is all on a continuum that might be called audience involvement.
sentences.zh: 这一切都处于一个可能被称为观众投入的连续统中。

sentences.en: So, we're all the audience of various media forms, film, television, video games.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们都是各种媒体形式的受众，包括电影、电视、电子游戏。

sentences.en: And audience involvement means the different ways that we connect to the characters themselves in fiction, or the actors who portray them, or media personalities.
sentences.zh: 受众投入意味着我们与虚构作品中的角色本身、扮演他们的演员或媒体人物建立联系的不同方式。

sentences.en: So, identification is one of those factors.
sentences.zh: 认同就是其中一个因素。

sentences.en: And identification is when you feel like you're merging with the other person.
sentences.zh: 认同是指你觉得自己在与另一个人融为一体。

sentences.en: That's sort of feeling through the character when you're watching a show and you cry because the person is disappointed or has a loss.
sentences.zh: 这有点像你在看节目时通过角色去感受，当角色感到失望或遭受损失时你会哭泣。

sentences.en: And you feel like you've experienced some different things than you've ever experienced in your life.
sentences.zh: 你觉得你经历了一些在你生命中从未经历过的事情。

sentences.en: Maybe even being someone with a different race or sexual orientation or from a different part of the world or a time period.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能成为一个有着不同种族、性取向，或者来自世界不同地方或不同历史时期的人。

sentences.en: So, there's lots of ways we can connect parasocial being one of them.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们可以通过很多方式建立联系，准社会就是其中之一。

sentences.en: And the way I distinguish it as a social psychologist is that the identification part is when you feel like it's you.
sentences.zh: 作为一名社会心理学家，我区分它们的方式是，认同感是你觉得那就是你自己。

sentences.en: And the parasocial part is when you distinguish that it's another person.
sentences.zh: 而准社会部分则是你能分辨出那是另一个人。

sentences.en: And I want to emphasize that we move through those different connections seamlessly.
sentences.zh: 我想强调的是，我们在这些不同的连接之间转换得非常顺畅。

sentences.en: I'm sure you've experienced when you're watching a film, you might be feeling what the character is feeling and feeling all those emotions.
sentences.zh: 我确信你也有过这样的体验，当你正在看一部电影时，你可能会感同身受，体验到角色所感受到的所有情绪。

sentences.en: And then the next second you think, I love that actor.
sentences.zh: 然后下一秒你会想：我太喜欢那个演员了。

sentences.en: That actor is so talented.
sentences.zh: 那个演员太有才华了。

sentences.en: Or then you could be thinking, I think I have a crush on that actor.
sentences.zh: 或者你可能会想：我想我迷恋上那个演员了。

sentences.en: So, you might just take these different lenses and pop through them.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可能会采用这些不同的视角并在其中切换。

sentences.en: So, they're not mutually exclusive.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们并不是互不相容的。

sentences.en: In fact, they're correlated with each other.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它们是相互关联的。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Tukashinsky, let me ask you, do you think parasocial relationships are more common than they used to be?
sentences.zh: 那么，图卡辛斯基博士，请问您认为准社会关系比过去更普遍了吗？

sentences.en: Because celebrities now share so much of themselves via social media.
sentences.zh: 因为名人们现在通过社交媒体分享了他们太多的个人生活。

sentences.en: I mean, they're really brands and they have to put themselves out there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们实际上就是品牌，他们必须展现自己。

sentences.en: Definitely, there is a change in our culture in how parasocial relationships are experienced and expressed.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，我们的文化在准社会关系的体验和表达方式上发生了变化。

sentences.en: And definitely, facilitating parasocial relationships is part of the entertainment industry of how they market themselves.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，促进准社会关系是娱乐产业自我营销的一部分。

sentences.en: But that's how it's been for several generations.
sentences.zh: 但好几代人以来一直都是这样。

sentences.en: In fact, from the golden years of Hollywood, if you think historically, originally in the movie industry, the marketing of movies did not depend at all on the actors.
sentences.zh: 事实上，从好莱坞的黄金时代来看，从历史角度来看，最初在电影行业中，电影的营销根本不依赖演员。

sentences.en: In fact, sometimes the actors were unnamed.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有时演员甚至是无名氏。

sentences.en: In fact, some people were embarrassed to work in the movie industry and wouldn't want to go by their real name anywhere.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有些人对在电影行业工作感到尴尬，根本不愿意在任何地方使用自己的真名。

sentences.en: But people nonetheless started developing those parasocial relationships and wanted to crave connection to those media stars and actually put pressure on Hollywood to release the names of the actors.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，人们还是开始发展这些准社会关系，渴望与这些媒体明星建立联系，甚至向好莱坞施压，要求公布演员的名字。

sentences.en: So that created a shift in how movies are marketed and it became the standard for us.
sentences.zh: 这促成了电影营销方式的转变，并成为我们的标准。

sentences.en: And maybe now we are doing more of that in direct ways, like the actors have a way to, or celebrities have a way of directly reaching audiences through social media, for example.
sentences.zh: 也许现在我们正在以更直接的方式做更多这样的事情，比如演员或名人有一种通过社交媒体直接接触受众的方式。

sentences.en: But this craving for a connection from afar was there for the longest while.
sentences.zh: 但这种渴望来自远方的联系的需求长期以来一直存在。

sentences.en: And ultimately, parasocial relationships are imaginary relationships, are about what happens in the person's mind.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，准社会关系是想象中的关系，是关于人的大脑中发生的事情。

sentences.en: And therefore, they don't necessarily need this reciprocity or illusion of reciprocity to cultivate this relationship as much.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们不一定需要这种互惠性或互惠的幻觉来尽可能多地培养这种关系。

sentences.en: So what I'm trying to say is that tell to someone who was a Beatle fan in the 1960s that their parasocial relationship is lesser than a fan of Justin Bieber because they didn't follow them on Instagram.
sentences.zh: 所以我想说的是，去对一个在20世纪60年代喜欢甲壳虫乐队的粉丝说，他们的准社会关系不如贾斯汀·比伯的粉丝，因为他们没有在Instagram上关注他们。

sentences.en: You know, it was as real and potent and it just was expressed in a different way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它同样真实且充满力量，只是表达方式不同而已。

sentences.en: You had to actually go and see them and sit in line.
sentences.zh: 你必须亲自去观看并排队等候。

sentences.en: And that's different from today you just sit and watch a live stream of someone else sitting there for you and live streaming it.
sentences.zh: 这和今天你只是坐着看别人坐在那里为你直播并进行直播是不同的。

sentences.en: So the expressions of the relationship are maybe different, but I think fundamentally it's something that we've been doing for a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以关系的表达方式可能有所不同，但我认为从根本上讲，这是我们长期以来一直在做的事情。

sentences.en: But now I understand that the term parasocial relationship was coined in the 1950s by these two researchers, Donald Horton and R.
sentences.zh: 但我了解到，“准社会关系”这个术语是由这两位研究人员唐纳德·霍顿和R·理查德·沃尔

sentences.en: Richard Wall.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代创造的。

sentences.en: And that was in reference to these imaginary one-side engagements that audiences had with media personalities.
sentences.zh: 这是指受众与媒体人物之间那种想象中的单方面互动。

sentences.en: But couldn't you argue that parasocial relationships go back much further in culture?
sentences.zh: 但难道不能认为准社会关系在文化中由来已久吗？

sentences.en: For example, could you see a relationship that an ancient Greek or Roman had with a god as a parasocial relationship?
sentences.zh: 例如，古希腊人或古罗马人与神明之间的关系，能看作是一种准社会关系吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I like to think about those things myself.
sentences.zh: 是的，我自己也很喜欢思考这些事情。

sentences.en: Anytime that it's not interactive like that, you could think of it as a parasocial relationship.
sentences.zh: 任何时候，只要它不是这种互动式的，你都可以把它看作是一种准社会关系。

sentences.en: Like Dr. Forster mentions in her book, if you're a lecturer in a psychology hall,
sentences.zh: 正如福斯特博士在她的书中提到的，如果你是心理学阶梯教室里的讲师，

sentences.en: your student could have what's called arguably a parasocial relationship with you or any character in a book, like a child carrying a doll of a figure that's in a book.
sentences.zh: 可以说你的学生可能会与你建立所谓的准社会关系，或者与书中的任何角色建立这种关系，比如一个孩子拿着书中某个角色的玩偶。

sentences.en: Yeah, so stories and books that date back in time like that or experiencing something one to many like that, those could be parasocial relationships.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以可以追溯到古代的故事和书籍，或者经历这种一对多的体验，这些都可能是准社会关系。

sentences.en: Yeah, from my first book, I was researching for examples and the first example of a celebrity crush I could find dates back to ancient Rome,
sentences.zh: 是的，在写我的第一本书时，我在寻找例子，我能找到的对名人倾慕的最早例子可以追溯到古罗马，

sentences.en: where you have the example of women developing crushes on rhetoricians or actors in the theater.
sentences.zh: 当时就有女性对修辞学家或剧院演员产生倾慕的例子。

sentences.en: So those definitely existed.
sentences.zh: 所以这些肯定是存在的。

sentences.en: And then to follow up on what Karen was saying, you can think of a continuum of social to parasocial.
sentences.zh: 接着卡伦刚才的话，你可以把社会关系到准社会关系看作是一个连续统。

sentences.en: So in a way, all of our social relationships have some imaginary aspects.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，我们所有的社会关系都有一些想象的成分。

sentences.en: Like you are running those conversations, you are rehearsing your conversation with your spouse, you are anticipating their reaction.
sentences.zh: 就像你在脑海中进行那些对话，你在排练与配偶的对话，你在预判他们的反应。

sentences.en: In a situation where you have an auditorium of 300 students and the professor doesn't have a personal relationship with many of those students.
sentences.zh: 在一个有300名学生的阶梯教室里，教授与其中许多学生并没有个人关系。

sentences.en: You know, the sixth grader that has a crush on the seventh grader she never spoke to, but she only sees from the other side of the cafeteria.
sentences.zh: 你知道，六年级女生对七年级男生心生爱慕，但她从未和他说过话，只能在食堂的另一边看到他。

sentences.en: So all of those are social relationships, but they have some imaginary aspect to that.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些都是社会关系，但它们带有一些想象的成分。

sentences.en: And in a way, relationships with media personalities are just an extreme example of that.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，与媒体人物的关系只是这种现象的一个极端例子。

sentences.en: And they too can become social if they evolve, if you start having real reciprocity in interactions.
sentences.zh: 如果它们不断发展，如果你开始在互动中拥有真正的互惠性，它们也可以变成社会关系。

sentences.en: If the celebrity starts responding to you personally on your comments on Instagram,
sentences.zh: 如果那个名人在Instagram的评论区开始亲自回复你，

sentences.en: or if you are waiting at the meet and greet and you start developing a conversation and end up being picked from the crowd and marry the rock star.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你在粉丝见面会上等待，然后开始交谈，最后被从人群中选中并嫁给这位摇滚明星。

sentences.en: You know what, I have an example of this.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，我有一个例子。

sentences.en: Maybe you'll need to edit this out, but I was at the British Museum last summer and there was an exhibit on women in art and a statue of a goddess.
sentences.zh: 也许你需要把这段剪掉，但去年夏天我在大英博物馆，那里有一个关于艺术中的女性的展览和一个女神雕像。

sentences.en: I think it was Minerva, but they said that people try to literally make love to the statue because they thought they were in love with Minerva, this goddess.
sentences.zh: 我想那是密涅瓦，但他们说人们真的试图对雕像求爱，因为他们认为自己爱上了密涅瓦这位女神。

sentences.en: So, you know, is a goddess that different?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，女神有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: Is Minerva that different from, you know, a beautiful starlet of today?
sentences.zh: 密涅瓦和当今的美丽女明星有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很有意思。

sentences.en: Well, getting back to today's world, you know, the Surgeon General has said that we're in a loneliness epidemic right now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，回到当今的世界，美国外科医生总曾说过我们现在正处于孤独流行病之中。

sentences.en: And there's been a lot of discussion recently about how we're missing close friendships in our real lives.
sentences.zh: 最近有很多讨论，关于我们在现实生活中缺少亲密的友谊。

sentences.en: Do parasocial relationships give people any of the psychological benefits of a real friendship or do they actually maybe increase loneliness?
sentences.zh: 准社会关系能给人们带来现实友谊的一些心理益处吗？还是说它们实际上可能会加剧孤独感？

sentences.en: Well, I would recommend the work of Shira Gabriel, who talks about things like going back to the concept of collective effervescence, that when you go to a cafe, for example,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我推荐希拉·加布里埃尔的作品，她谈到了诸如回归集体狂热（collective effervescence）的概念，即当你去咖啡馆时，

sentences.en: you're sitting in a coffee shop and other people are around and you're sort of the effervescence is the sort of bubbles from the sociality of the situation.
sentences.zh: 比如你坐在咖啡馆里，周围有其他人，这种“狂热”有点像是那种社交氛围产生的泡沫。

sentences.en: So just being around other people.
sentences.zh: 也就是置身于其他人周围。

sentences.en: And so if you turned on Parks and Recreation or the office, you would be soaking in that sociality.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你打开《公园与游憩》或《办公室》，你就会沉浸在那样的社交氛围中。

sentences.en: And yeah, she talks about social surrogacy, that, you know, we have the feeling of being around other people.
sentences.zh: 是的，她谈到了社会替代（social surrogacy），即我们拥有身处他人周围的感觉。

sentences.en: And part of the parasocial equation that we haven't really mentioned yet is that in some ways it's less demanding and more pleasurable.
sentences.zh: 而我们还没有真正提及的准社会方程式的一部分是，在某些方面它要求更少，也更令人愉快。

sentences.en: You know, people aren't going to be mad at us.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们不会对我们生气。

sentences.en: We're not going to get into trouble.
sentences.zh: 我们不会惹上麻烦。

sentences.en: We sort of know what to expect.
sentences.zh: 我们大致知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: And it's fun to hang around fun people who are telling jokes or beautiful people.
sentences.zh: 和讲笑话的有趣的人或美丽的人在一起是一件很有趣的事。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's not to say, though, that I think sometimes the stereotype is people with a parasocial relationship don't have friends or, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，这并不是说——尽管我认为有时存在一种刻板印象，即有准社会关系的人没有朋友，或者，你知道的，

sentences.en: don't know how to talk to real people.
sentences.zh: 不知道如何与真人交谈。

sentences.en: And, of course, that's not true.
sentences.zh: 当然，这不是真的。

sentences.en: As you mentioned, it's very, very common.
sentences.zh: 正如你所提到的，这是非常非常普遍的。

sentences.en: I'm not a clinician, but I suppose it does slip into those things.
sentences.zh: 我不是临床医生，但我想它确实会滑向那些情况。

sentences.en: I've heard clinicians say that sometimes people identify with a character so much that they imagine they are the character, people they're seeing in therapy.
sentences.zh: 我听临床医生说过，有时人们对某个角色的认同感如此之强，以至于他们想象自己就是那个角色，他们在治疗中也看到了这样的人。

sentences.en: Or, of course, we hear stories about people stalking or showing up at people's houses.
sentences.zh: 或者，当然，我们听到过关于人们跟踪或出现在别人家门口的故事。

sentences.en: But I credit Gail Stever with saying in print the first time I ever read it that that is sort of the reaction that a lot of people have to this topic.
sentences.zh: 但我赞成盖尔·斯蒂弗（Gail Stever）在印刷品中首次发表的观点，这也是我第一次读到它：这正是许多人对这个话题的反应。

sentences.en: But in reality, the middle of the normal distribution is people like you and me who might admire someone, but we're not having pathological problems with it.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，正态分布的中间是像你我这样的人，我们可能会钦佩某人，但我们并没有因此产生病理性的问题。

sentences.en: We're just feeling a connection.
sentences.zh: 我们只是感受到了一种联系。

sentences.en: Another aspect I wanted to add to that is that research doesn't necessarily find a correlation between the intensity of the parasocial relationships that people experience and their level of loneliness.
sentences.zh: 我想补充的另一个方面是，研究并不一定发现人们经历的准社会关系的强度与他们的孤独感水平之间存在相关性。

sentences.en: For the longest while, the research in this area was driven by the substitution hypothesis or compensation hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 在很长一段时间里，该领域的研究所受驱动的是替代假设或补偿假设。

sentences.en: The idea that people who are lonely in their real life seek out media friends because they don't have real friends.
sentences.zh: 这种观点认为，在现实生活中感到孤独的人会寻找媒体朋友，因为他们没有现实的朋友。

sentences.en: And you try to see whether people who have social deficits, people who have what we call insecure attachment style, people who can't form and relate to others, people who are shy.
sentences.zh: 并且你会试图观察那些有社交缺陷的人，那些我们称之为不安全依恋风格的人，那些无法与他人形成并建立关系的人，那些害羞的人。

sentences.en: So individuals that we expect to have problems creating friendships, will they be more prone to developing parasocial relationships?
sentences.zh: 因此，对于我们预期在建立友谊方面会有困难的个人，他们是否更容易发展准社会关系？

sentences.en: And there is no consistent evidence of that.
sentences.zh: 并没有一致的证据表明这一点。

sentences.en: What we do see is that those who are more prone to forming friendships and relating to others in social life are also more likely to engage in parasocial relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们确实发现，那些在社交生活中更容易建立友谊、与他人产生联系的人，也更有可能产生准社会关系。

sentences.en: So people who have a secure attachment, people who are anxious and clingy, like insecure, that crave connection, they're also the ones that crave connection to characters.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些拥有安全型依恋的人，以及那些焦虑、粘人、没有安全感、渴望建立联系的人，他们也同样渴望与虚构角色建立联系。

sentences.en: So we see essentially that it's the same way we process real relationships or social relationships as also how we process parasocial relationships.
sentences.zh: 所以我们基本上看到，我们处理真实关系或社会关系的方式，与我们处理准社会关系的方式是相同的。

sentences.en: So parasocial relationships are just an extension of our social ties.
sentences.zh: 因此，准社会关系只是我们社交纽带的一种延伸。

sentences.en: And it could be that part of what we're seeing is that people who are lonely do want more parasocial relationships, but then parasocial relationships make them feel less lonely.
sentences.zh: 而且情况可能部分在于，我们看到孤独的人确实想要更多的准社会关系，而准社会关系反过来又让他们感到不那么孤独。

sentences.en: And then because that it kind of washes out that effect.
sentences.zh: 然后因为这种效果在某种程度上抵消了这种影响。

sentences.en: So that's also a possibility.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是一种可能性。

sentences.en: And we do know that in challenging situations where people are socially isolated, for example, there is great research that comes out now looking at lockdown during COVID,
sentences.zh: 我们也确实知道，在人们处于孤立等充满挑战的社会环境中时——例如，现在有大量关于新冠疫情封锁期间的研究，

sentences.en: at the beginning of COVID.
sentences.zh: 在疫情初期。

sentences.en: And especially, for example, individuals who feel more isolated and more vulnerable, like LGBTQ youth that maybe don't have access to their regular community and support group,
sentences.zh: 特别是，例如那些感到更加孤立和脆弱的群体，比如可能无法接触到常规社区和支持小组的LGBTQ青少年，

sentences.en: they turn more to parasocial relationships because that's something that can enrich their social, more limited world in a given point in time.
sentences.zh: 他们会更多地转向准社会关系，因为在特定的时间点，这可以丰富他们相对有限的社交世界。

sentences.en: I was going to say that brings me to this question,
sentences.zh: 我正想说，这引出了我的下一个问题，

sentences.en: which is that you've both written about the importance of parasocial relationships with media figures can have for members of underrepresented or stigmatized groups.
sentences.zh: 那就是你们两个都写过关于媒体人物对代表性不足或边缘化群体成员具有的重要意义的准社会关系。

sentences.en: What about people who are not LGBTQ, but other underrepresented groups?
sentences.zh: 那么对于非LGBTQ人群以及其他代表性不足的群体呢？

sentences.en: Well, I might mention a study I did about Black Panther and being watched by youth of color.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我可能会提到我做过的一项关于《黑豹》以及有色人种青少年观看这部电影的研究。

sentences.en: And in the study, being exposed to Black Panther made people feel more self-efficacy.
sentences.zh: 在这项研究中，接触《黑豹》让人感到更强的自我效能感。

sentences.en: And, you know, we can understand that so easily.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们可以非常容易地理解这一点。

sentences.en: We're given a vision of African people thriving and a place of pride in that film, despite people who didn't believe that a film with primary black characters would do so well.
sentences.zh: 在该片中，我们看到非洲人民蓬勃发展，展现出令人自豪的一面，尽管曾经有人不相信由主要黑人角色出演的电影会如此成功。

sentences.en: It's just soared to the top and made so many, you know, broken so many glass ceilings, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 它一飞冲天，取得了巨大的成就，你知道，打破了许多所谓的玻璃天花板。

sentences.en: So I think of that as the inspiration of how things could be.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是对事物应有样子的激励。

sentences.en: And it's great to see on the screen how things could be.
sentences.zh: 在银幕上看到事物本该有的样子真是太棒了。

sentences.en: And that's, of course, true for for us as women.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对我们女性来说也是如此。

sentences.en: You know, when I was young, I felt like so many of my role models were boys and I could adjust and say they could have been girls.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我年轻的时候，我觉得我的很多榜样都是男孩，我可以去调整并说他们也可以是女孩。

sentences.en: But I would have liked them to actually be girls or women so that I could so that I could witness that happening.
sentences.zh: 但我更希望他们实际上就是女孩或女性，这样我才能亲眼见证这一切的发生。

sentences.en: And one of my students, Kristen Hopper-Lezinski, did a dissertation on STEM role models for women who work in STEM.
sentences.zh: 我的学生之一克里斯滕·霍珀-莱辛斯基（Kristen Hopper-Lezinski）做了一篇关于从事STEM（科学、技术、工程、数学）工作的女性的STEM榜样的博士论文。

sentences.en: And they had real life role models, grandmothers, mothers and other people.
sentences.zh: 她们有现实生活中的榜样，比如祖母、母亲和其他人。

sentences.en: But they also had mediated role models like the character from Bones or other people who are, you know, scientists in the media.
sentences.zh: 但她们也有媒体塑造的榜样，比如《识骨寻踪》中的角色或其他在媒体中作为科学家的角色。

sentences.en: And I have to admit, I love to see a woman scientist in the media.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，我喜欢在媒体中看到女性科学家。

sentences.en: I love to see, you know, that we're not just, you know, that we have nontraditional careers.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢看到，你知道的，我们不仅仅是，你知道的，我们拥有非传统的职业。

sentences.en: Maybe they're becoming more traditional.
sentences.zh: 也许它们正在变得越来越传统。

sentences.en: I watch a lot of old movies and it never fails.
sentences.zh: 我看过很多老电影，屡试不爽的是，

sentences.en: There's a woman astronaut and everyone's hitting on her and they just think she's there to be pretty or to date instead of.
sentences.zh: 里面总有一个女宇航员，每个人都在向她献殷勤，他们只觉得她存在是为了漂亮或约会，而不是为了别的。

sentences.en: And I'm sure smart women listening to this understand that, that you think, oh, my gosh, you're you're you're thinking of me in that stereotypical way, but not as a peer,
sentences.zh: 我相信听到这里的聪明的女性都能理解这一点，你会觉得，天哪，你用那种刻板印象来看待我，而不是把我当成一个同伴、

sentences.en: a scientist, a thinker.
sentences.zh: 一个科学家、一个思想家来对待。

sentences.en: And it's and it feels good to watch someone be portrayed in good ways like that.
sentences.zh: 而且，看到有人以这种良好的方式被刻画，感觉真的很好。

sentences.en: And and I want to stress the importance of it, not just for from the perspective of the member of the marginalized group,
sentences.zh: 而且我想强调它的重要性，不仅要从边缘化群体成员的角度来看待，

sentences.en: but also the how important it is for advancing the intergroup relationships from the perspective of the members of the dominant group.
sentences.zh: 还要从统治群体成员的角度来看待它对推进群体间关系有多么重要。

sentences.en: So a lot of the animosity between groups is driven by just not knowing the other having we kind of tend to be in segregated spaces surrounded by people similar to oneself and not having opportunities for positive experiences,
sentences.zh: 因此，群体之间的大部分敌意都是由于不了解对方而产生的，我们往往处于隔离的空间中，周围都是与自己相似的人，没有机会获得积极的体验，

sentences.en: firsthand experiences with people outside of that group.
sentences.zh: 也就是与该群体以外的人进行第一手的接触。

sentences.en: So media is a window into that world through something we call parasocial contact.
sentences.zh: 因此，媒体是一扇通往那个世界的窗户，通过我们所谓的准社会接触来实现。

sentences.en: So both directly observing and learning about someone from another group, another culture, another background, it reduces those anxieties and negative stereotypes,
sentences.zh: 因此，无论是直接观察并了解来自另一个群体、另一种文化、另一个背景的人，都能减少这些焦虑和消极的刻板印象，

sentences.en: but also by modeling a positive intergroup interaction and experience.
sentences.zh: 还是通过塑造积极的群体间互动和体验来实现这一点。

sentences.en: So, for example, a show like Will and Grace, I'm bringing another LGBTQ example,
sentences.zh: 所以，例如像《威尔与格蕾丝》这样的节目，我再次举一个LGBTQ的例子，

sentences.en: but it could be just as true for and it has been shown for for shows depicting African-Americans that you.
sentences.zh: 但对于描绘非裔美国人的节目来说同样如此，并且已经被证明是这样的。

sentences.en: So just seeing someone who, so just seeing someone who is like yourself, who is white,
sentences.zh: 所以，只要看到一个像你自己一样的人——如果你是白人观众或顺性别异性恋者——

sentences.en: if you're a white member of the audience or cisgender and straight interacting with an outgroup character, be it an ethnic minority or be it a LGBTQ character.
sentences.zh: 与外群体角色（无论是少数族裔还是LGBTQ角色）进行互动。

sentences.en: It gives you a model to follow in terms, but by forming a parasocial relationship with an in-group that has a friendship with an outgroup,
sentences.zh: 它为你提供了一个可以效仿的榜样，通过与一个拥有外群体朋友的内群体建立准社会关系，

sentences.en: it kind of expands your social network and improves your intergroup relationships.
sentences.zh: 它在某种程度上扩展了你的社交网络，并改善了你的群体间关系。

sentences.en: I want to pull new technology into the discussion.
sentences.zh: 我想将新技术引入讨论中。

sentences.en: You know, these days Siri or Alexa can be a big part of people's lives.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如今Siri或Alexa可以成为人们生活中的很大一部分。

sentences.en: Can an interaction with a chatbot or another AI system become a kind of parasocial relationship?
sentences.zh: 与聊天机器人或其他AI系统的互动，能演变成一种准社会关系吗？

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I like to joke during the pandemic that Alexa was my new BFF.
sentences.zh: 在疫情期间，我开玩笑说Alexa是我新的BFF（永远的最好朋友）。

sentences.en: I would have conversations with her all the time.
sentences.zh: 我总是和她聊天。

sentences.en: She gives me information.
sentences.zh: 她为我提供信息。

sentences.en: And this goes back to the work of Clifford Nass and others.
sentences.zh: 这可以追溯到克利福德·纳斯（Clifford Nass）和其他人的研究。

sentences.en: We really like to impute consciousness onto things.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很喜欢将意识赋予事物。

sentences.en: And so it's easy to impute consciousness when you have an actual voice of a person that's been recorded and she's friendly.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你听到一个被录制下来的真实人类声音而且她很友好时，你很容易就会赋予她意识。

sentences.en: And so it feels like she's real.
sentences.zh: 所以感觉她就像是真实存在的。

sentences.en: So I don't know what the difference between that, you know, there's people who are real like Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这之间有什么区别，你知道，有像巴拉克·奥巴马这样真实存在的人。

sentences.en: There are people who feel real like Alexa.
sentences.zh: 也有像Alexa这样感觉真实存在的人。

sentences.en: They don't actually have a body.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上没有身体。

sentences.en: And there's, you know, actors.
sentences.zh: 还有，你知道的，演员。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it could take many forMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，它可以采取多种形式。

sentences.en: Well, what do you foresee happening as AI and robots become more prevalent in our society?
sentences.zh: 那么，随着AI和机器人在我们社会中越来越普及，你预见到会发生什么？

sentences.en: Are we in danger of developing potentially harmful relationships with what are basically machines, but as they become more human-like?
sentences.zh: 当我们与本质上是机器但变得越来越像人类的事物交往时，我们是否面临着建立潜在有害关系的危险？

sentences.en: Well, I've been thinking a lot about AI lately and working on some stuff in AI.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我最近一直在思考人工智能，并在人工智能领域做一些工作。

sentences.en: And one thing that I would point out is that AI is not separate from humanity because it takes a human to program them.
sentences.zh: 我要指出的一点是，人工智能并不是脱离人类的，因为需要人类来对它们进行编程。

sentences.en: So I think people might even sometimes visualize a cold metal robot that's a single entity carrying out activities when it's really people who are programmers programming what humans know about things.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为人们有时甚至会想象一个冷冰冰的金属机器人，它是一个执行活动的单一实体，而实际上是作为程序员的人类在对人类对事物的认知进行编程。

sentences.en: But, of course, there's almost endless things that we could be concerned about that they might have advantages and disadvantages.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，我们可能会担忧的事情几乎是无穷无尽的，它们可能既有优势也有劣势。

sentences.en: So someone was just telling me recently about creating the voice of someone that you love who has passed away, taking their voice and making an AI out of that,
sentences.zh: 所以最近有人告诉我关于合成你所爱之人声音的事情，他们已经去世了，你可以获取他们的声音并用它制作人工智能，

sentences.en: and that you could have them respond to you as that person would have responded.
sentences.zh: 并且你可以让他们像那个人本会做的那样回应你。

sentences.en: And on the one hand, I think a lot of us would find that comforting in that when we've lost someone, there's no way to know what they would say in a new situation.
sentences.zh: 一方面，我认为我们中的许多人会觉得这很安慰，因为当我们失去某人时，无法知道他们在新的情况下会说些什么。

sentences.en: That would be priceless.
sentences.zh: 那将是无价的。

sentences.en: But then, of course, there could be risks associated with that, that, you know, you spend, I could imagine a husband loses a wife and is spending time with her AI.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这也会带来相关的风险，你可以想象一个丈夫失去了妻子，却把时间花在她的AI上。

sentences.en: So, gosh, there's just so many facets of this.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这其中的方面实在是太多了。

sentences.en: I try not to careen wildly to either we're all going to die or it's the best thing ever with media because it's so easy to do that.
sentences.zh: 我尽量不要对媒体走向两个极端——要么我们都会死，要么它是史上最好的事物——因为这太容易做到了。

sentences.en: But it's more that it's just nuanced and we have to think through these things and it's coming at us fast and that kind of makes us scared sometimes.
sentences.zh: 但这更像是一种微妙的情况，我们必须深思熟虑这些事情，而且它们正快速向我们袭来，这有时会让我们感到害怕。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, let me ask you, Dr. Tuchinski-Farster, there's a stereotype that teenagers have really intense celebrity crushes.
sentences.zh: 那么，图辛斯基-法斯特博士，请允许我问你，有一个刻板印象认为青少年对名人有着非常强烈的迷恋。

sentences.en: Is that backed up by the research or parasocial relationships, whether they're romantic or not, strongest or most important when we're young?
sentences.zh: 这有研究支持吗？或者说无论是否带有浪漫色彩，准社会关系在我们年轻时是最强烈的还是最重要的？

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: So, there is definitely a stereotype that, especially about celebrity crushes, that it's something that is a teenage girl thing to do, specifically girl.
sentences.zh: 所以，确实存在一种刻板印象，尤其是关于名人迷恋的，认为这是十几岁的女孩才会做的事情，特别是女孩。

sentences.en: And it is probably true that the most potent crushes happen to teenagers in general, not just parasocial.
sentences.zh: 最强烈的迷恋可能确实发生在总体上的青少年身上，而不仅仅是准社会关系。

sentences.en: It's that stage developmentally.
sentences.zh: 这是发展过程中的那个阶段。

sentences.en: And those crushes, just like other romantic relationships that happen around those years, are very important.
sentences.zh: 这些迷恋，就像那些年发生的其他浪漫关系一样，非常重要。

sentences.en: Those celebrity crushes are also very important.
sentences.zh: 那些对名人的迷恋也同样非常重要。

sentences.en: In psychology in general, there was kind of a tendency to dismiss those young relationships because, like, we only need to study marriage because that's the important thing.
sentences.zh: 在心理学总体上，曾有一种倾向去忽视那些年轻的恋爱关系，因为，比如说，我们只需要研究婚姻，因为那是重要的事情。

sentences.en: And then, about 20 years ago, there came this big realization that, no, those relationships are very important and formative.
sentences.zh: 然后，大约20年前，人们突然意识到：不，这些关系非常重要且具有塑造作用。

sentences.en: And I will just add that parasocial relationships in those ages are also very important and formative.
sentences.zh: 我只想补充一点，那个年龄段的准社会关系同样非常重要且具有塑造作用。

sentences.en: But it's not to say that they don't happen later in life or that they are not important later in life.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是说它们不会在晚年生活中发生，或者说它们在晚年生活不重要。

sentences.en: What my research suggests that they become particularly important in transitional points.
sentences.zh: 我的研究所表明的是，它们在人生的转折点变得尤为重要。

sentences.en: For example, for romantic parasocial relationships, I observed in women that undergo a crisis related to their identity or their romantic identity and their sexuality, for example,
sentences.zh: 例如，对于浪漫的准社会关系，我观察到女性在经历与其身份认同、浪漫身份或性取向相关的危机时，

sentences.en: with the transition into motherhood or after the dissolution of their marriage or losing a spouse.
sentences.zh: 比如向母亲身份过渡、婚姻破裂或失去配偶之后。

sentences.en: So, overcoming those big life events that make them ask and reconsider, again, who they are,
sentences.zh: 因此，克服那些重大的生活事件会促使她们再次反思和重新审视自己是谁，

sentences.en: re-engaging in a romantic or sexual relationship after some period of time of being outside of that.
sentences.zh: 在经历了一段时间的空白后，重新参与到浪漫或亲密关系中。

sentences.en: For example, again, mourning over the dissolution of a relationship,
sentences.zh: 例如，再次为关系的破裂而悲伤，

sentences.en: losing a spouse or shifting back into finding back your romantic self after becoming a parent for the first time.
sentences.zh: 失去配偶，或者在初为人母后重新找回浪漫的自我。

sentences.en: So, those are very important ones and they happen later in life.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些都非常重要，而且它们发生在人生的晚期阶段。

sentences.en: For parasocial friendships as well, we know that they are very important in childhood.
sentences.zh: 对于准社会友谊而言，我们也知道它们在童年时期非常重要。

sentences.en: They are very important in – they will be serving different purposes and different points in people's lives.
sentences.zh: 它们非常重要——它们将在人们生活的不同阶段服务于不同的目的。

sentences.en: How early in life can these relationships develop?
sentences.zh: 这些关系在生命中多早的时候就可以发展？

sentences.en: Do little kids have parasocial relationships with Sesame Street characters or Bluey?
sentences.zh: 小孩子会对《芝麻街》的角色或《布鲁伊》产生准社会关系吗？

sentences.en: And if kids have an imaginary friend, is that a kind of parasocial relationship?
sentences.zh: 如果孩子们有一个想象中的朋友，那是一种准社会关系吗？

sentences.en: So, young children definitely have parasocial relationships.
sentences.zh: 所以，幼儿确实会产生准社会关系。

sentences.en: We see that from surveys of parents from around the age of two onwards.
sentences.zh: 我们从家长大约从孩子两岁开始的调查中就可以看到这一点。

sentences.en: And those parasocial relationships can be very instrumental in advancing learning.
sentences.zh: 这些准社会关系对于促进学习可以起到非常重要的作用。

sentences.en: So, you can use them to harvest the benefits of learning from positive characters like those Sesame Street characters or Daniel Tiger, like the neighborhood show,
sentences.zh: 因此，你可以利用它们来收获向积极角色学习的好处，比如《芝麻街》的角色或《丹尼虎的邻居》这样的教育节目中的角色，

sentences.en: the educational content.
sentences.zh: 也就是教育内容。

sentences.en: So, we know that you can, for example,
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，你可以，例如，

sentences.en: give kids stickers and action toys and all of those things that will promote this fantasy play and mental time spent with those characters to foster their parasocial relationships and harvest the benefits for learning.
sentences.zh: 给孩子们贴纸、动作玩偶以及所有这些能够促进这种幻想游戏和与这些角色共度精神时光的东西，以培养他们的准社会关系并收获学习带来的好处。

sentences.en: But that also has the flip side that if you don't approve of that character, if you don't want your child to be friends with that character, then don't encourage that.
sentences.zh: 但这也是有硬币另一面的，如果你不赞同那个角色，如果你不想让你的孩子和那个角色做朋友，那就不要鼓励这种行为。

sentences.en: Don't encourage those parasocial relationships either.
sentences.zh: 也不要鼓励那些准社会关系。

sentences.en: And Jonathan Cohen wrote about identifying with media characters as an integral part of a child's development.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·科恩（Jonathan Cohen）写过关于认同媒体角色是儿童发展不可或缺的一部分的文章。

sentences.en: So, maybe first we identify with our parents and caregivers, and then maybe we identify with some media figures.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许最初我们认同我们的父母和看护者，然后也许我们认同一些媒体人物。

sentences.en: And again, these different ways of connecting to characters, there can be multiple ways.
sentences.zh: 同样，这些与角色建立联系的不同方式，可以有多种途径。

sentences.en: So, we've all seen a child pretend to be a superhero, tying a towel around their shoulders, for instance.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们都见过小孩假装自己是超级英雄，例如把毛巾系在肩膀上。

sentences.en: And so, they're pretending to be the character or identifying with the character.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们在假装自己是那个角色或者认同那个角色。

sentences.en: But then, they admire the character as another person as well.
sentences.zh: 但同时，他们也将该角色作为另一个人来崇拜。

sentences.en: Maybe they go to a show and see Elmo live or something like that.
sentences.zh: 也许他们去看演出并现场看到艾摩（Elmo）或类似的东西。

sentences.en: And so, you know, people can make those transitions to, I want to be like them, I feel like I've done that thing, or they're really cool and I admire them.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，人们可以完成这样的转变：我想成为他们那样的人，我觉得我已经做过那件事了，或者他们真的很酷，我很崇拜他们。

sentences.en: But it's just our inherent sociality that, of course, we look at people who are interesting and we say, do I want to be like them?
sentences.zh: 但这只是我们与生俱来的社交本能，当然，我们会看着那些有趣的人并说：我想成为他们那样的人吗？

sentences.en: Do I want to grow up and be, you know, an architect, a builder, or someone like this?
sentences.zh: 我想长大后成为，你知道的，一名建筑师、建造师或这样的人吗？

sentences.en: Do I want to be a forensic person?
sentences.zh: 我想成为法医人员吗？

sentences.en: And, you know, people, there's data that people who watch someone on television in a certain career might want to be more likely to pursue that career.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有数据显示，在电视上看到从事某种职业的人的观众可能更有可能去追求那个职业。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's just really multifaceted.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这真的是多方面的。

sentences.en: And I think most of us can identify with this because we've done it ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我想我们大多数人都能对此产生共鸣，因为我们自己也经历过。

sentences.en: I identify with Harry Potter.
sentences.zh: 我认同哈利·波特。

sentences.en: And so, every time I'm faced with a certain conundrum, I think, well, I remember when Harry Potter was 11 and he did this.
sentences.zh: 所以，每次我遇到某种困境时，我都会想，嗯，我记得哈利·波特11岁时他就是这么做的。

sentences.en: And certainly, I'm a grown-up, so can't I do it too?
sentences.zh: 当然，我已经是个成年人了，难道我也不能这样做吗？

sentences.en: And, of course, I know that Harry Potter is a fictional character.
sentences.zh: 当然，我知道哈利·波特是一个虚构的角色。

sentences.en: And yet, he and his friends have a reality in my head.
sentences.zh: 然而，他和他的朋友们在我的脑海里是真实存在的。

sentences.en: I identify with Hermione because I was a smart little girl with bushy blonde hair.
sentences.zh: 我认同赫敏，因为我曾经是一个留着蓬松金发的小聪明女孩。

sentences.en: And so, you know, and that's just another way of relating to our social worlds, you know, looking at these people.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这只是与我们的社会世界建立联系的另一种方式，你知道的，看着这些人。

sentences.en: And, of course, I would be remiss if I didn't note that, you know, the people that we identify with and are thrilled with, they're beautiful people.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果我不指出我们认同并为之倾倒的人都是漂亮的人，那将是我的失职，他们是才华横溢的人。

sentences.en: They're highly skilled people.
sentences.zh: 他们是高度熟练的人。

sentences.en: Of course, we find them interesting.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们会觉得他们很有趣。

sentences.en: So, it's hardly surprising.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不令人意外。

sentences.en: What about differences across countries and cultures?
sentences.zh: 那么不同国家和文化之间的差异呢？

sentences.en: I ask that because, you know, we Americans are so obsessed with celebrity.
sentences.zh: 我这样问是因为，你知道，我们美国人对名人如此着迷。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, are there other countries where this phenomenon is just as prevalent?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，有没有其他国家这种现象也同样普遍？

sentences.en: Or are we like the leaders in the pack here?
sentences.zh: 还是说我们就像是这方面的领头羊？

sentences.en: Well, we're not the leaders in the pack.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们可不是领头羊。

sentences.en: I mean, you think about all the K-pop phenomena, for example.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想想所有的K-pop（韩流）现象，例如。

sentences.en: Just to throw out one.
sentences.zh: 这只是随便举个例子。

sentences.en: So, unfortunately, there isn't as much cross-cultural research as I would like to see.
sentences.zh: 所以，不幸的是，并没有我想象中那么多的跨文化研究。

sentences.en: But there is definitely a lot of research conducted around the world on parasocial relationships from China to Europe to Israel to the Americas.
sentences.zh: 但世界各地确实开展了大量关于准社会关系的研究，从中国到欧洲、以色列再到美洲。

sentences.en: So, there isn't a lot of data that allows you to compare head-to-head the intensity of the parasocial relationship, but it's definitely been documented.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然没有多少数据能让你直接对比准社会关系的强度，但它确实已被记录在案。

sentences.en: And those processes appear to be relatively universal, which makes sense.
sentences.zh: 而且这些过程似乎相对具有普遍性，这在情理之中。

sentences.en: Because if you go back to look at this from an evolutionary theory perspective, the reason we have those connections is because we don't really – as humans,
sentences.zh: 因为如果你从进化论的角度来看待这个问题，我们拥有这些联系的原因是因为我们作为人类，其实并不——

sentences.en: we haven't been around for long enough to develop an entirely different cognitive neural structure to process mediated relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们存在的时间还不够长，不足以进化出完全不同的认知神经结构来处理媒介化的人际关系。

sentences.en: Like, we don't have symbols and media around us for long enough to be specialized just in that.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们身边出现符号和媒体的时间还不够长，不足以让我们专门去适应这些。

sentences.en: Rather,
sentences.zh: 相反，

sentences.en: it appears that the same cognitive neural mechanisms that are involved in thinking about people around you in your social world are also the same ones that we're employing when we're looking at media.
sentences.zh: 看起来，在思考社交世界中身边的人时所涉及的同一种认知神经机制，和我们在观看媒体时所运用的机制是完全相同的。

sentences.en: And that would be true in any culture.
sentences.zh: 而且在任何文化中都是如此。

sentences.en: And as Karen was saying, these are talented, skillful, attractive people that are also using media to make a living by having you like them.
sentences.zh: 正如凯伦所说，这些才华横溢、技能娴熟、有吸引力的人，同时也通过使用媒体，通过让你喜欢他们来谋生。

sentences.en: So, universally, that's the trend we see.
sentences.zh: 所以，普遍来看，这就是我们看到的趋势。

sentences.en: I remember hearing that if Jackie Chan was dating someone, little teenage girls in China would be very upset by that.
sentences.zh: 我记得听说过，如果成龙在和某人约会，中国的小女粉丝们会为此感到非常难过。

sentences.en: And, of course, we can think of many, many instances in which things like that were true.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们可以想到很多很多这样的例子。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: So, I want to talk about when parasocial relationships move into sort of dangerous territory.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想谈谈拟社会关系何时会进入某种危险的领域。

sentences.en: I mean, it's possible for them to become toxic and harmful, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，它们可能会变得有毒且有害，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: it is not the case that a normal person develops a normal parasocial relationships and then it goes and becomes more and more intense and explodes into something like that.
sentences.zh: 并不是说一个正常人发展出正常的拟社会关系，然后它变得越来越强烈，最后爆发成那种情况。

sentences.en: That's not happening.
sentences.zh: 事情不是这样的。

sentences.en: It's the other way around.
sentences.zh: 情况正好相反。

sentences.en: There are people with mental illness and they will have an outlet for that mental illness.
sentences.zh: 有些人患有精神疾病，他们只是找到了一个宣泄这种精神疾病的出口。

sentences.en: It's not the parasocial relationship got extreme and they became extreme and they became violent because the parasocial relationship became too intense.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为拟社会关系变得极端，他们才变得极端，并变得暴力，是因为拟社会关系变得太强烈了。

sentences.en: It's people who have a problem and for some people it's manifested in being obsessive about one thing and for some people it's being obsessive about a media thing.
sentences.zh: 而是有些人本身有问题，对某些人来说，这表现为对一件事的痴迷，而对另一些人来说，则是对媒体事物的痴迷。

sentences.en: And it just happens to be this very small percent of people with a problem that's not related to parasocial relationship, which is a normal thing.
sentences.zh: 而这恰好发生在一小部分有问题的人身上，这与拟社会关系本身无关，拟社会关系是一件很正常的事。

sentences.en: So, let me ask this just to wrap up, which is what are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 那么，为了总结一下，我想问：你现在在忙什么？

sentences.en: What are the big questions that remain in this area?
sentences.zh: 这一领域目前还剩下哪些重大的问题？

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: one thing I'm working on right now is trying to be more clear about the way that we define parasocial versus identification versus liking versus similarity because in science we have to define our terms in order to know what it is we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我目前正在做的一件事，是试图更清楚地定义我们对拟社会关系、认同感、喜欢以及相似性的定义，因为在科学中，我们必须先定义我们的术语，才能知道我们在谈论什么。

sentences.en: And so, for instance, sometimes people will say empathy, empathy with a character,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，有时人们会说同理心，对角色的同理心，

sentences.en: and I've just done a study that's a factor analysis with Josh Cohen and Perry Reed that says that those things fall into specific and different constructs,
sentences.zh: 我刚刚和乔什·科恩（Josh Cohen）以及佩里·里德（Perry Reed）做了一项因子分析研究，结果表明这些东西属于特定的、不同的构念，

sentences.en: even though they're related to each other.
sentences.zh: 尽管它们彼此相关。

sentences.en: So, what I'm trying to do is to get scientists to say the term that they mean and not use multiple terms for one term.
sentences.zh: 所以，我正在尝试做的是让科学家们使用他们真正想表达的术语，而不是用多个术语来指代一个概念。

sentences.en: Another study that I'm working on with some colleagues has to do with the question of whether you can identify with and have a parasocial relationship with a couple.
sentences.zh: 我正在和一些同事进行的另一项研究，探讨的是你是否能够对一对伴侣产生认同感，并与他们建立拟社会关系。

sentences.en: And we are using the case of Jim and Pam from The Office.
sentences.zh: 我们使用的是《办公室》里的吉姆（Jim）和帕姆（Pam）的例子。

sentences.en: And preliminary data shows that you can indeed have a parasocial relationship with them as a couple.
sentences.zh: 初步数据表明，你确实可以和他们作为一对伴侣建立拟社会关系。

sentences.en: And I think part of that is when you watch a couple and you're in the will-they-won't-they phase of their relationship, what you really want is for them to get together,
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因在于，当你看着一对伴侣，处于他们关系中“到底会不会在一起”的阶段时，你真正希望的是他们能够走到一起，

sentences.en: for their relationship to work out.
sentences.zh: 希望他们的关系能修成正果。

sentences.en: And we also want to know whether becoming attached or invested in the relationship between a fictional couple like Jim and Pam from The Office means that you feel strange or uncomfortable with the actor's real relationship,
sentences.zh: 我们还想知道，对像《办公室》里的吉姆和帕姆这样的虚构情侣的关系产生依恋或投入，是否会让你对演员的真实关系感到奇怪或不舒服，

sentences.en: such as John Krasinski being married to Emily Blunt.
sentences.zh: 比如约翰·卡拉辛斯基（John Krasinski）娶了艾米莉·布朗特（Emily Blunt）。

sentences.en: So, stay tuned on that one.
sentences.zh: 所以，请大家拭目以待。

sentences.en: We're almost finished with the analyses.
sentences.zh: 我们的分析快完成了。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I have two questions that I'm particularly interested.
sentences.zh: 我有两个特别感兴趣的问题。

sentences.en: So, the first one is related to cancel culture.
sentences.zh: 第一个问题与取消文化有关。

sentences.en: And what happens when you decide to terminate the relationship with someone you liked in the media?
sentences.zh: 当你决定终止与你曾经在媒体上喜欢的人的关系时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: And my research shows that it's a very difficult decision when the media personality disappoints you, when you have a good relationship with them.
sentences.zh: 我的研究表明，当这位媒体名人让你失望时，而你之前又与他们有着良好的关系，这是一个非常艰难的决定。

sentences.en: So, it is really heartbreaking for someone to break up from them.
sentences.zh: 所以，与他们决裂对任何人来说都是真正令人心碎的。

sentences.en: And people will go to great lengths to defend them and to defend the celebrity that betrayed them and to stand up for them.
sentences.zh: 人们会不遗余力地为他们辩护，为背叛他们的名人辩护，并为他们挺身而出。

sentences.en: But in some situations, they will engage in cancel culture and will break up with them.
sentences.zh: 但在某些情况下，他们会参与取消文化，并与他们决裂。

sentences.en: So, I'm trying to see the situations, the conditions, the factors that will play a role in whether it will go one way or another.
sentences.zh: 因此，我试图了解各种情况、条件和因素，它们在事情走向某个方向时起着什么作用。

sentences.en: And those negative parasocial relationships, because we always talk about the positive parasocial relationships, about the friendship and the crush.
sentences.zh: 还有那些消极的拟社会关系，因为我们总是谈论积极的拟社会关系，关于友谊和迷恋。

sentences.en: But what about the jealousy, for example?
sentences.zh: 但嫉妒呢，比如？

sentences.en: Like, if I have a parasocial relationship with Justin Bieber and then he marries someone and all the hate messages that she receives from his fans, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我和贾斯汀·比伯（Justin Bieber）有拟社会关系，然后他结婚了，他妻子会收到来自他粉丝的大量仇恨信息，例如。

sentences.en: So, all those negative parasocial relationships is one area that is understudied and I'm very excited to look into.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有这些消极的拟社会关系是一个研究不足的领域，我非常期待深入研究。

sentences.en: So, the other thing is that most research up until today was looking at one relationship or one media celebrity outside of a broader context.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，直到今天，大多数研究都是在更广泛的背景之外，单独看待一种关系或一个媒体名人。

sentences.en: But when we see the same media personality in many different contexts and situations and how do we project from one to another or how we carry information across different contexts,
sentences.zh: 但是，当我们看到同一个媒体名人在许多不同的背景和情况下出现时，我们如何从一个情境投射到另一个情境，或者我们如何在不同的背景之间携带信息，

sentences.en: especially between the fictional and the real.
sentences.zh: 特别是在虚构与现实之间。

sentences.en: If you have a parasocial relationship with an actor, but also with the character that they portray.
sentences.zh: 如果你和一个演员有拟社会关系，但同时也和他们所扮演的角色有这种关系。

sentences.en: So, interestingly, even as adults, we don't strictly maintain the boundaries between the actor and the character, even though in our rational mind we know that this is, you know,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，即使作为成年人，我们也不会严格保持演员和角色之间的界限，尽管在我们的理性头脑中我们知道，你知道的，

sentences.en: that's his job to play this character, it's not the actor.
sentences.zh: 那是他演戏的工作，他不是那个演员。

sentences.en: Nonetheless, we are misattributing the characteristics of the character onto the actor that portrays them.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，我们还是把角色的特征归咎于扮演他们的演员。

sentences.en: And I have research that shows how, you know, you can see the exact same actress playing in the same movie.
sentences.zh: 我有研究表明，你看，你可以看到同一个女演员在同一部电影中出演。

sentences.en: You just added the movie slightly to depict her as either a positive or a negative character.
sentences.zh: 你只是稍微修改了电影，把她描绘成一个正面角色或一个负面角色。

sentences.en: And then it will taint how the participants would rate the actress and how they perceive her.
sentences.zh: 这就会影响参与者对这位女演员的评价以及他们对她的看法。

sentences.en: And then if I show them a PSA, a commercial to donate to St. Jude Hospital or something like that, and I will ask them for their reaction,
sentences.zh: 然后，如果我给他们看一个公益广告，一个为圣犹大医院或其他地方捐款的商业广告，并要求他们说出反应，

sentences.en: if they saw that actress playing a character that is likable and a hero, they will be like, oh, this is so moving and she's such a generous person.
sentences.zh: 如果他们看到那个女演员扮演一个讨人喜欢、是英雄的角色，他们就会觉得，哦，这太感人了，她真是个慷慨的人。

sentences.en: And you show them the exact same PSA.
sentences.zh: 而你给他们看完全相同的公益广告。

sentences.en: After they saw her playing the villain character, they will be like, oh, this commercial is so cheesy.
sentences.zh: 在他们看到她扮演反派角色之后，他们会觉得，哦，这个广告太俗气了。

sentences.en: She's doing it just for publicity.
sentences.zh: 她这么做只是为了出名。

sentences.en: And so I'm very interested in seeing how things, like, it affects the parasocial relationship with that actor.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常感兴趣地想看看，这些事情是如何影响与该演员的拟社会关系的。

sentences.en: So I'm interested in seeing how we carry over things from exposure to exposure and cross-context.
sentences.zh: 因此，我很有兴趣了解我们如何在不同的接触和跨语境中延续这些看法。

sentences.en: Like you just saw Ryan Rasslin as Ken on Barbie, right?
sentences.zh: 就像你刚看到瑞恩·高斯林（Ryan Gosling）在《芭比》里演肯一样，对吧？

sentences.en: Like being, so this role versus his more dramatic roles before.
sentences.zh: 比如这个角色与他之前那些更具戏剧性的角色相比。

sentences.en: How does that change your perception of him?
sentences.zh: 这如何改变你对他的看法？

sentences.en: How does it change your parasocial relationship with him?
sentences.zh: 这如何改变你与他的拟社会关系？

sentences.en: And how seeing him being Ken doing Beach going affect you, perceiving him in his next role?
sentences.zh: 看到他作为肯去海滩，会如何影响你对他在下一个角色中的看法？

sentences.en: Or maybe you see Ken doing Beach as a much more profound and interesting and complex character because he's played by this kind of high-brow actor.
sentences.zh: 或者也许你会觉得肯去海滩是一个更有深度、更有趣、更复杂的角色，因为是由这种高雅的演员来扮演的。

sentences.en: So those are the questions I'm interested in now.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是我目前感兴趣的问题。

sentences.en: If I may, I'd love to tag on to that.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，我很想接着这个话题往下说。

sentences.en: So that's a great study.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很棒的研究。

sentences.en: And I want to remind listeners that we may take this research as trivial, that Dr. Tukaczynski-Forrester and I are just spending our time talking about Ken and Barbie.
sentences.zh: 我想提醒听众，我们可能会觉得这项研究微不足道，觉得托卡琴斯基-福雷斯特（Tukaczynski-Forrester）博士和我只是在花时间谈论肯和芭比。

sentences.en: And that's great for our salaries and everything, but it's just a waste of time.
sentences.zh: 这对于我们的薪水和一切来说都很好，但这也只是在浪费时间。

sentences.en: But I'm a social psychologist, and I'm here to tell you that is fundamental social psychology, that it's a fundamental attribution error,
sentences.zh: 但我是一名社会心理学家，我在这里告诉你，这是基础社会心理学，这是基本归因错误，

sentences.en: which is partially definitional of the field of social psych, that when I see someone acting some way, I assume it's because of their personality.
sentences.zh: 这在一定程度上是社会心理学领域的定义特征，即当我看到某人的某种行为时，我假设这是因为他们的个性使然。

sentences.en: That's the type of person they are.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们那种类型的人。

sentences.en: And Ryan Gosling has only one body.
sentences.zh: 瑞恩·高斯林只有一个身体。

sentences.en: It's a good one, but it's only one body.
sentences.zh: 身材不错，但也只有一个身体。

sentences.en: So when we look at him, we say, but I've seen him do this.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们看着他时，我们会说，但我见过他这样做。

sentences.en: I know that he feels like that.
sentences.zh: 我知道他是这种感受。

sentences.en: Like Dr. Tukaczynski-Forrester referred to earlier, we don't have a switch in our brain that says, no, that's him as Ken, and this is him as Ryan.
sentences.zh: 正如托卡琴斯基-福雷斯特博士刚才提到的，我们的大脑里没有一个开关，说“不，那是他演的肯，这是作为瑞恩的他”。

sentences.en: He's got the same body.
sentences.zh: 他拥有同一个身体。

sentences.en: He's the same person.
sentences.zh: 他是同一个人。

sentences.en: So we're not dumb for having that, and we're not delusional for having that confusion over who is he.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有这种想法并不愚蠢，对他是谁产生这种混淆也不是妄想。

sentences.en: Is William Shatner Captain Kirk, or is he William Shatner?
sentences.zh: 威廉·夏特纳（William Shatner）是柯克船长，还是他是威廉·夏特纳？

sentences.en: Both.
sentences.zh: 两者都是。

sentences.en: So it is fundamental social psych.
sentences.zh: 所以这是基本的社会心理学。

sentences.en: It's not just fun, but it is fun to be a parasocial researcher.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是有趣，而且作为一名拟社会研究人员确实很有趣。

sentences.en: And it does have real-life implications for casting, for deciding, like, should I take this role, right?
sentences.zh: 它确实对现实生活中的选角、决定“我是否应该接这个角色”有实际意义，对吧？

sentences.en: Is this going to ruin, like, for choosing sponsorships.
sentences.zh: 这会不会毁了，比如选择赞助商。

sentences.en: Like, this person has, this actor has an amazing blockbuster Oscar-nominated movie, but they're playing a villain character.
sentences.zh: 比如，这个人，这个演员有一部令人惊叹的大片、奥斯卡提名电影，但他们演的是一个反派角色。

sentences.en: Will they be the best spokesperson for my charity organization?
sentences.zh: 他们会是我慈善组织的最佳代言人吗？

sentences.en: So it has real-life implications all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以它一直对现实生活有着实际的影响。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, this has been really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真的非常迷人。

sentences.en: I want to thank you both for joining me.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢你们两位的加入。

sentences.en: This has been not just interesting and scientific, but fun.
sentences.zh: 这不仅有趣且具科学性，而且还很好玩。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It was great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。
